reading: The all-black grid gets a one-cell frame of colour 8 along its border; the inside stays 0.

new_rows.name: gborder
new_rows.datalog:
maxy(max(Y)) :- px(Y, X, C).
maxx(max(X)) :- px(Y, X, C).
gborder(Y, X) :- px(Y, X, C), Y = 0.
gborder(Y, X) :- px(Y, X, C), X = 0.
gborder(Y, X) :- px(Y, X, C), maxy(M), Y = M.
gborder(Y, X) :- px(Y, X, C), maxx(M), X = M.

why: every grid-border cell becomes 8; interior cells unchanged

reading: The colour run at the start of the middle row is repeated cyclically along that row at positions 0,1,3,6,10,15,... (gaps grow by one each step).

slots.sequence: the contiguous colour run starting at column 0 of the middle row
slots.positions: triangular numbers k(k+1)/2 for k=0,1,2,... while inside the row
slots.colour: the k-th placed cell takes sequence[k mod len(sequence)]

why: on every pair the non-zero cells of the output row sit exactly at triangular-number columns, colours cycling through the seed run
invariants: rows other than the middle row stay 0

reading: A full line of 1 holds some 8 and 2 cells; from each, a stalk grows upward: under a top cell of the same colour, 8 gets 2 cells of 1 (height 3) and 2 gets 3 cells of 1 (height 4).

slots.line: the one full row of non-background cells (mostly 1)
slots.sources: cells of the line whose colour is not 1 (8 or 2)
slots.length: colour-dependent: 8 -> 3 cells, 2 -> 4 cells, going up from the line
slots.body: cells between line and tip are colour 1
slots.tip: top cell of the stalk takes the source colour

why: each stalk sits directly above its source cell, its length set by the source colour (8:3, 2:4)

reading: Every 4 drops one row. A 4 that lands right on top of the 2-line shoots diagonal rays of 4 up-left and up-right to the grid border.

new_rows.name: landed
new_rows.datalog: landed(Y, X) :- px(Y, X, 4), Y2 = Y + 1, px(Y2, X, 2).

why: all 4 cells shift down by exactly one row; rays (two diagonals going upward) start only at 4s whose cell below is 2 and run to the border

reading: A top-row segment and a bottom-row segment of one colour face a full 2 row. In the columns both segments share, the cells between the separator and the longer segment become 4.

new_rows.name: bridge
new_rows.datalog:
maxy(max(Y)) :- px(Y, X, C).
maxx(max(X)) :- px(Y, X, C).
rowcnt(Y, count(X)) :- cell(Y, X, C).
sep(Y) :- rowcnt(Y, N), maxx(MX), N = MX + 1, Y > 0, maxy(M), Y < M.
topn(count(X)) :- cell(Y, X, C), Y = 0.
botn(count(X)) :- cell(Y, X, C), maxy(M), Y = M.
ovl(X) :- cell(Y1, X, C1), Y1 = 0, cell(Y2, X, C2), maxy(M), Y2 = M.
bridge(Y, X) :- ovl(X), px(Y, X, 0), sep(S), topn(A), botn(B), A > B, Y > 0, Y < S.
bridge(Y, X) :- ovl(X), px(Y, X, 0), sep(S), maxy(M), topn(A), botn(B), B > A, Y > S, Y < M.

why: filled cells are exactly the overlap columns on the longer segment's side of the separator, colour 4

reading: A ragged line of 2 crosses the grid. In each column, everything above the line becomes 0 and everything below becomes the noise colour; the 2s stay.

new_rows.name: below
new_rows.datalog:
bot2(X, max(Y)) :- px(Y, X, 2).
below(Y, X) :- px(Y, X, C), bot2(X, B), Y > B.

new_rows.name: above
new_rows.datalog:
has2(Y, X) :- px(Y, X, 2).
has2(Y, X) :- px(Y, X, C), px(Y2, X, 2), Y2 < Y.
above(Y, X) :- px(Y, X, C), !has2(Y, X).

why: per column, cells below the lowest 2 take the pair's non-2 foreground colour (1, 5, 8) and cells above the highest 2 (or the whole column if it has no 2) become 0

reading: Several V-shaped 2 containers and some loose 9 cells. The container whose inside (background cells between its arms, row by row) holds exactly as many cells as there are loose 9s is filled with 9, and the loose 9s are erased.

slots.capacity: count of background cells lying between the object's own cells on each of its rows
slots.markers: the loose cells of the other colour
slots.target: the container whose capacity equals the marker count
slots.action: fill the target's inside with the marker colour; erase the markers

why: marker count equals the capacity of exactly one container on each pair (1 and 4), and only that one is filled

reading: A 7x7 key panel of 1 has four coloured cells at its inner corners. Each 3x3 shape whose colour is in the key is copied into a 7x7 output, into the corner quadrant where the key shows that colour. Other shapes are dropped.

slots.key: the 7x7 colour-1 panel; its cells at (1,1),(1,5),(5,1),(5,5) name the colour for each quadrant
slots.pieces: single-colour objects outside the panel, each fitting a 3x3 box
slots.output: 7x7 of 0; quadrant boxes at rows/cols 0-2 and 4-6, row 3 and col 3 empty
slots.placement: piece of colour c goes, keeping its shape in its 3x3 box, to the quadrant whose key cell is c; pieces of colours not in the key are dropped

why: each output quadrant equals the 3x3 box of the shape coloured like the matching key corner

reading: Stripes of 8 separated by 0 lines contain one 2x2 block of 6. In every other stripe, the 8 cells beyond a widening cone around the 6 block become 4. The cone is 2 cells wide one stripe away and grows by 2 cells on each side per further stripe.

new_rows.name: cone
new_rows.datalog:
y0(min(Y)) :- px(Y, X, 6).
y1(max(Y)) :- px(Y, X, 6).
x0(min(X)) :- px(Y, X, 6).
x1(max(X)) :- px(Y, X, 6).
maxy(max(Y)) :- px(Y, X, C).
fullrow(Y) :- px(Y, X, 8).
fullrow(Y) :- px(Y, X, 6).
hz(K) :- px(Y, X, C), Y > 0, maxy(M), Y < M, !fullrow(Y), K = 1.
vt(K) :- px(Y, X, C), K = 1, !hz(K).
ry(Y, D) :- px(Y, X, C), y0(A), Y < A, D = A - Y.
ry(Y, D) :- px(Y, X, C), y1(B), Y > B, D = Y - B.
ry(Y, D) :- px(Y, X, C), y0(A), y1(B), Y >= A, Y <= B, D = 0.
rx(X, D) :- px(Y, X, C), x0(A), X < A, D = A - X.
rx(X, D) :- px(Y, X, C), x1(B), X > B, D = X - B.
rx(X, D) :- px(Y, X, C), x0(A), x1(B), X >= A, X <= B, D = 0.
cone(Y, X) :- hz(K), px(Y, X, 8), ry(Y, D), D > 0, rx(X, F), L = 3 * F, R = 2 * D - 3, L >= R.
cone(Y, X) :- vt(K), px(Y, X, 8), rx(X, D), D > 0, ry(Y, F), L = 3 * F, R = 2 * D - 3, L >= R.

why: only 8 cells change, all to 4, exactly those outside the cone; the 6 block's own stripe, the 0 cells and the 6 block are untouched

reading: A wall line (frame edge) has a key line just inside it, and a parallel line of marks lies outside it. Each mark equal to the key cell in its row or column moves next to the wall. Each mark that differs moves to the far grid border. The mark line is cleared.

slots.wall: the full single-colour non-background line (row 7 of 0s; column 2 of 4s)
slots.key: the line adjacent to the wall on the frame side
slots.marks: non-background cells on the open side of the wall, all in one line parallel to it
slots.match: mark colour equals the key cell aligned with it across the wall
slots.action: matching mark moves to the cell adjacent to the wall; non-matching mark moves to the grid border on the open side; original mark positions become background

why: on every pair each mark stays in its own column/row and lands either touching the wall (key match) or on the far border (mismatch)
invariants: marks keep their colour and their column/row
